Heard learned counsel for the revisionist and learned counsel for the State.

2. The present criminal revision application has been filed against the order dated 01.12.2023,
passed by the court of learned Additional Principal Judge, Additional Family Court No.2,
Jamshedpur, in Original Maintenance Case No.216 of 2018, whereby maintenance of Rs.25,000/-
per month has been awarded to the wife/ O.P. No.02.
3.

Additional Principal Judge, Additional Family Court No.2,
Jamshedpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: It has been submitted by the learned counsel for the revisionist/ husband that the wife has left the matrimonial home without any reasonable cause and as such she is not entitled for maintenance.

It has further been submitted that a case under Section 498A of the I.P.C has been lodged against the revisionist which has resulted in acquittal and as such there is no reason for residing separately.

entities.text: Jahar Lal Dutta Aged About 55 Years Son Of ... vs The State Of Jharkhand
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Having heard learned counsel for the revisionist and from perusal of record, it appears that it is the second marriage of the revisionist.
As per his claim, the first wife has left and thereafter, he has performed the second marriage.
They have lived like husband and wife, but they have not been blessed with any child.
There is allegation of handing over the house of the father -in- law and there is other allegations also.
After evaluating the evidence brought on record, the family court has found that the wife has a reasonable reason for residing separately.
Further, the income of the husband has been found more than one lakh per month and accordingly, the order of maintenance has been passed.
5. Considering the above fact, I find no reason to entertain the present criminal revision application.

Accordingly, the same is, hereby, dismissed.
6.
Pending interlocutory application, if any, stands disposed of.

(Rajesh Kumar, J.) Chandan/-
